subject: geography
title: Food Security and the FAO
welcome_lead: From cereal stockpiles to dietary diversity — explore the meaning and measurement of food security.
meta_desc: Geography Adventure: food security, FAO definitions and global hunger.
final_note: You have measured food security. Both production and access matter; both can fail.

concepts.def: FAO definition: when all people have physical, social and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food at all times.
Average daily kilocalories per person available for human consumption in a country.
Extreme food crisis classified as IPC Phase 5, with widespread starvation and excess mortality.
Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN, headquartered in Rome.
Composite measure including undernourishment, child stunting, wasting and mortality.

walkthroughs.body_html: The FAO's four pillars — availability (supply), access (purchasing power), utilisation (nutrition, water, sanitation) and stability (resilience to shocks) — guide both analysis and policy. A country may produce enough food yet have widespread food insecurity if access is unequal.

DES is reported by FAO; world average is around 2,900 kcal/person/day, but minimum dietary energy requirement varies by demographics (~1,800-2,100 kcal). The Global Hunger Index combines undernourishment, child stunting, wasting and child mortality.

The proportion of undernourished people fell from about 19% in 1990 to around 9% in 2015 but has risen again with COVID-19, conflict (Ukraine, Sudan) and climate shocks. The FAO estimated about 735 million people undernourished in 2022, with food insecurity especially acute in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

mcqs.q: Why does longshore drift move sediment in only one direction along a coast?
options: Longshore drift moves sediment back and forth with the tide.
Stacks form when the sea level rises and floods a hill.
Longshore drift only happens during storms.
The prevailing wind drives swash diagonally up the beach at an angle, but gravity-driven backwash returns sediment straight downhill — creating net movement in the swash direction.

mcqs.q: What is the sequence of headland erosion from crack to stump?
options: Stacks form when the sea level rises and floods a hill.
Crack to cave to arch to stack to stump — waves widen cracks into caves, two caves meet to form an arch, the arch collapses leaving a stack, and the stack erodes to a stump.
Stacks form where rocks fall from the cliff into the sea.
Lag time is the delay between thunder and lightning.

options: The time between peak rainfall and peak river discharge — affected by drainage basin shape, land use, soil saturation and vegetation.
